Four waterbodies had established quagga populations, while the remaining two did not, despite suspected opportunities for introduction. Using data reduction techniques and an advanced machine learning (ML) classification algorithm, gradient boosted machine, we identified environmental and ecological conditions that differentiated established from negative stations. Notably, parameters considered crucial to dreissenid invasion (e.g., calcium, alkalinity, temperature, dissolved oxygen) were not among the most important variables to classification, as all examined waterbodies exhibited quagga-suitable ranges. Rather, in this system, the established class was characterized by conditions linked to dreissenid osmoregulation and indicators of primary productivity and trophic state. Further, established stations had lower zooplankton abundances of dreissenid competitors and prey, perhaps resulting from food competition and consumption, respectively. Notably, negative waterbodies, Bartlett Reservoir and Theodore Roosevelt Lake, exhibited different biotic and abiotic conditions from each other. Our study demonstrates that negative waterbodies with suitable calcium concentrations may still have differing invasion risks.","catalogStatusId":1,"metadataFilePath":null,"metadataStandard":{"_id":"ISO","definition":"International Standards Organization (ISO) 19115-1:2014 metadata content standard, and ISO 19139:2007 metadata implementation standard","createDate":"2018-11-20T13:25:52+00:00"},"createDate":"2024-09-05T21:29:56+00:00","updateDate":"2026-09-09T19:51:04+00:00","programNames":["Science and Technology Program"],"generationEffort":"S\u0026T Project 21086:Machine Learning Can Refine Models of Environmental Suitability and Ecological Associations for Invasive Quagga Mussels","generationEffortId":414,"subTheme":{"_id":5,"subTheme":"Invasive Species Monitoring","definition":"Relating to surveys of the presence and\/or characteristics of one or more invasive animal or plant species","createDate":"2018-11-14T14:35:10+00:00"},"tags":["Dreissenid Mussels","Aquatic Invasive Species","Decision Trees","Partial Dependence"],"themes":["Biological"]},"relationships":{"location":{"data":{"type":"Location","id":"\/rise\/api\/location\/7081"}},"catalogItems":{"data":[{"type":"CatalogItem","id":"\/rise\/api\/catalog-item\/128739"}]}}},{"id":"\/rise\/api\/catalog-record\/8577","type":"CatalogRecord","attributes":{"_id":8577,"recordTitle":"Cascade Reservoir Operations Pilot: Evaluating Operational Alternatives to Reduce Harmful Algae in Cascade Reservoir, Idaho, 2018-2022","recordDescription":"This reservoir operations pilot study explored the potential effects that theoretical changes in operations of reservoirs in the upper Payette River basin might have on reducing harmful algal blooms in Cascade Reservoir. River and reservoir operations models, coupled with a newly developed water quality model for Cascade Reservoir were used to simulate a range of operational alternatives and the potential effects on harmful algal blooms. The water quality model, CE-QUAL-W2, is a two-dimensional (longitudinal-vertical) laterally averaged water quality and hydrodynamic model for rivers, estuaries, lakes, reservoirs and river basin systems. The model for Cascade Reservoir was developed in coordination with Portland State University (PSU). This record includes a model archive containing the model files and data needed to rerun the models and reproduce the results for the model scenarios considered by the larger study. The model archive includes 1) the original model files produced by PSU, 2) the installation file for the version of the CE-QUAL-W2 software used for this study, 3) model input and configuration files for the scenarios considered by the study, and 4) the tools used to summarize the results. The station is in Socorro, New Mexico. The associated instruments deploy automatically to monitor river stage, flow velocity, and bedload flux, which includes acoustic impacts as a surrogate for bedload, narrow-band and broad-band seismic sensors as a surrogate for bedload, suspended sediment concentration (SSC), and turbidity as a surrogate for SSC. Four waterbodies had established quagga populations, while the remaining two did not, despite suspected opportunities for introduction. Using data reduction techniques and an advanced machine learning (ML) classification algorithm, gradient boosted machine, we identified environmental and ecological conditions that differentiated established from negative stations. Notably, parameters considered crucial to dreissenid invasion (e.g., calcium, alkalinity, temperature, dissolved oxygen) were not among the most important variables to classification, as all examined waterbodies exhibited quagga-suitable ranges. Rather, in this system, the established class was characterized by conditions linked to dreissenid osmoregulation and indicators of primary productivity and trophic state. Further, established stations had lower zooplankton abundances of dreissenid competitors and prey, perhaps resulting from food competition and consumption, respectively. Notably, negative waterbodies, Bartlett Reservoir and Theodore Roosevelt Lake, exhibited different biotic and abiotic conditions from each other. River and reservoir operations models, coupled with a newly developed water quality model for Cascade Reservoir were used to simulate a range of operational alternatives and the potential effects on harmful algal blooms. The water quality model, CE-QUAL-W2, is a two-dimensional (longitudinal-vertical) laterally averaged water quality and hydrodynamic model for rivers, estuaries, lakes, reservoirs and river basin systems. The model for Cascade Reservoir was developed in coordination with Portland State University (PSU). This record includes a model archive containing the model files and data needed to rerun the models and reproduce the results for the model scenarios considered by the larger study. The station is in Socorro, New Mexico. The associated instruments deploy automatically to monitor river stage, flow velocity, and bedload flux, which includes acoustic impacts as a surrogate for bedload, narrow-band and broad-band seismic sensors as a surrogate for bedload, suspended sediment concentration (SSC), and turbidity as a surrogate for SSC. Acoustic impact sensors have faced challenges at the ADLP. Notwithstanding, data from the impact sensors are calibrated to sediment flux with promising success. Fluvial seismology is a growing area of research, and the ADLP station and the Arroyo de los Montoyas are on the cutting edge. <section class="wp-block-taa-blocks-section has-large-margin-top has-large-margin-bottom"><div class="">
<div class="header-with-subtitle"><h2 class="bordered-title" style="color:#19304b" data-aos="true">Check out our new FishNV tool</h2></div>



<article class="undefined text-block-with-image" style="background:linear-gradient(to bottom, #ffffff 20.5%, #ffddc4 20.5%)"><figure class="wp-block-image text-block-with-image__image"><picture><img decoding="async" width="2160" height="1080" class="wp-image-2441 large" loading="lazy" src="https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content.jpg" alt="" srcset="https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content.jpg 2160w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content-992x496.jpg 992w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content-1440x720.jpg 1440w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content-768x384.jpg 768w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content-1536x768.jpg 1536w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content-2048x1024.jpg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2160px) 100vw, 2160px" /></picture></figure><div class="text-block-with-image__content"><div class="text-block-with-image__inner" style="background-color:#ffddc4"><div class="text-block-with-image__text">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Fishing Nevada waters is a great pastime with many unique spots across the state. Did you know that NDOW staff has built a tool to help anglers like you get to know Nevada waters and the species living in them? In this interactive map, you can look through the species found in Nevada and see which bodies of water they reside in. Check out our new interactive FishNV tool.</p>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tal"><a href="https://fish.wildlifenv.com/" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Explore FishNV Here</a></div>
</div></div></div></article>
</div></section>



<section class="wp-block-taa-blocks-section has-large-margin-top "><div class="">
<div class="header-with-subtitle"><h2 class="bordered-title" style="color:#19304b" data-aos="true">Where do I start?</h2></div>



<article class="undefined text-block-with-image" style="background:none"><figure class="wp-block-image text-block-with-image__image"><picture><img decoding="async" width="2160" height="1080" class="wp-image-2445 large" loading="lazy" src="https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy.jpg" alt="" srcset="https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy.jpg 2160w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy-992x496.jpg 992w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy-1440x720.jpg 1440w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy-768x384.jpg 768w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy-1536x768.jpg 1536w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy-2048x1024.jpg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2160px) 100vw, 2160px" /></picture></figure><div class="text-block-with-image__content"><div class="text-block-with-image__inner" style="background-color:#ffffff"><div class="text-block-with-image__text">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">All you need to fish Nevada waters is a pole and a license. Buy your annual or single day license today to get out and explore beautiful parts of the state.</p>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tac"><a href="http://www.ndowlicensing.com" class="cta cta--orange " style="background-color: #e58947">Buy a license now</a></div>



<div class="preparation-plan"><div class="preparation-plan__intro tac"></div><div class="preparation-plan__list accordion">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-accordion-item accordion__item" data-acc="cb53658f-a1e2-4cc4-b84a-8818f209bce5" data-bg="#589fd6" data-aos="" id="accodrion-0"><details><summary>Research </summary><div>
<p class="has-large-font-size wp-block-paragraph">Learn more about fishing in Nevada and how to plan out your trip whether you are new or an experienced angler.</p>



<div class="grid grid--2 grid--small-padding">
<div class="grid__item" data-aos="fade-up">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tal"><a href="/get-outside/fishing/plan-your-fishing-trip" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Plan</a></div>
</div>



<div class="grid__item" data-aos="fade-up">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tal"><a href="/get-outside/fishing/fishing-stocking-reports" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Latest Reports</a></div>
</div>



<div class="grid__item" data-aos="fade-up">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tal"><a href="/species-information" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Find Species</a></div>
</div>



<div class="grid__item" data-aos="fade-up">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tal"><a href="https://fish.wildlifenv.com/" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Interactive Map</a></div>
</div>
</div>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-accordion-item accordion__item" data-acc="6040e164-f39f-44c2-8ed1-798fd4fc37dc" data-bg="#589fd6" data-aos="" id="accodrion-2"><details><summary>Eligibility</summary><div>
<p class="has-large-font-size wp-block-paragraph">People of all ages are allowed to head out to the waters to catch a fish, but anyone 12 years of age or older is required to have a fishing license in their possession while in the field.</p>



<p class="has-large-font-size wp-block-paragraph">If you don’t plan to fish but will be assisting someone (no matter the age), you will be required to have a fishing license.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-accordion-item accordion__item" data-acc="9dcff40d-1570-4a09-965f-e78dcf4d050f" data-bg="#589fd6" data-aos="" id="accodrion-1"><details><summary>License Costs </summary><div>
<p class="activity-list-item__text wp-block-paragraph">Licenses can be purchased online any time of year to head out and fish. License fees are listed below.</p>



<h5 id="specialty-combination-licenses-verification-required" class="wp-block-heading has-small-margin-bottom has-s-m-margin-top has-navy-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-1">Resident Fishing licenses</h5>



<div class="wp-block-group is-nowrap is-layout-flex wp-container-core-group-is-layout-7387b849 wp-block-group-is-layout-flex">
<figure class="wp-block-table has-medium-margin-bottom is-style-regular"><table><tbody><tr><td>Annual Adult Hunt & Fish<br>Combination License <br>(ages 18 & older)</td><td>$75.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Adult Fishing License <br>(ages 18 & older)</td><td>$40.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Youth Hunt & Fish<br>Combination License<br>(ages 12-17)</td><td>$15.00</td></tr><tr><td>1-Day Fishing Permit<br>(ages 18 & older)</td><td>$9.00</td></tr><tr><td>1-Day Fishing Permit<br>Consecutive Day</td><td>$3.00</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>
</div>



<h5 id="nonresident-tag-costs" class="wp-block-heading has-small-margin-bottom has-s-m-margin-top has-navy-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-2">Nonresident fishing licenses</h5>



<div class="wp-block-group is-nowrap is-layout-flex wp-container-core-group-is-layout-7387b849 wp-block-group-is-layout-flex">
<figure class="wp-block-table has-medium-margin-bottom"><table><tbody><tr><td>Annual Adult Fishing License<br>(ages 18 & older)</td><td>$80.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Youth Hunt & Fish <br>Combination License<br>(ages 12-17)</td><td>$15.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Nevada Interstate <br>Boundary Waters License</td><td>$30.00</td></tr><tr><td>1-Day Fishing Permit<br>(ages 18 & older)</td><td>$18.00</td></tr><tr><td>1-Day Fishing Permit<br>Consecutive Day</td><td>$7.00</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>
</div>



<h5 id="nonresident-tag-costs" class="wp-block-heading has-small-margin-bottom has-s-m-margin-top has-navy-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-3">resident Specialty fishing licenses</h5>



<div class="wp-block-group is-nowrap is-layout-flex wp-container-core-group-is-layout-7387b849 wp-block-group-is-layout-flex">
<figure class="wp-block-table has-medium-margin-bottom"><table><tbody><tr><td>Annual Senior Specialty <br>Hunt & Fish Combination License<br>(age 65+ with 6 months residency)</td><td>$15.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Serviceman Specialty <br>Hunt & Fish Combination License*</td><td>$15.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Severely Disabled Specialty<br>Hunt & Fish Combination License**</td><td>$15.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Disabled Veteran Specialty <br>Hunt & Fish Combination License**</td><td>$15.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Native American Specialty <br>Hunt & Fish Combination License**</td><td>$10.00</td></tr></tbody></table><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">*Available at NDOW offices only<br>**Initial application must be processed at an NDOW office</figcaption></figure>
</div>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Note: Prices do not include nominal processing fee</p>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tac"><a href="https://nevada.licensing.kalkomey.com/licenses" class="cta cta--orange " style="background-color: #e58947">Buy a license now</a></div>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-accordion-item accordion__item" data-acc="d30bf119-2213-4672-a3c1-81e8e2df8d21" data-bg="#589fd6" data-aos="" id="accodrion-3"><details><summary>Fishing Limits & Seasons </summary><div>
<p class="activity-list-item__text wp-block-paragraph">Find the most recent fishing limits and seasons in your area.</p>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tal"><a href="https://www.eregulations.com/nevada/fishing " class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Fishing Regulation Book through E-Regulations</a></div>
</div></details></div>
</div></div>

<article class="undefined text-block-with-image" style="background:linear-gradient(to bottom, #ffffff 20.5%, #ffddc4 20.5%)"><figure class="wp-block-image text-block-with-image__image"><picture><img decoding="async" width="2160" height="1080" class="wp-image-2441 large" loading="lazy" src="https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content.jpg" alt="" srcset="https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content.jpg 2160w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content-992x496.jpg 992w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content-1440x720.jpg 1440w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content-768x384.jpg 768w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content-1536x768.jpg 1536w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fish-shock-content-2048x1024.jpg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2160px) 100vw, 2160px" /></picture></figure><div class="text-block-with-image__content"><div class="text-block-with-image__inner" style="background-color:#ffddc4"><div class="text-block-with-image__text">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Fishing Nevada waters is a great pastime with many unique spots across the state. Did you know that NDOW staff has built a tool to help anglers like you get to know Nevada waters and the species living in them? In this interactive map, you can look through the species found in Nevada and see which bodies of water they reside in. Check out our new interactive FishNV tool.</p>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tal"><a href="https://fish.wildlifenv.com/" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Explore FishNV Here</a></div>
</div></div></div></article>
</div></section>



<section class="wp-block-taa-blocks-section has-large-margin-top "><div class="">
<div class="header-with-subtitle"><h2 class="bordered-title" style="color:#19304b" data-aos="true">Where do I start?</h2></div>



<article class="undefined text-block-with-image" style="background:none"><figure class="wp-block-image text-block-with-image__image"><picture><img decoding="async" width="2160" height="1080" class="wp-image-2445 large" loading="lazy" src="https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy.jpg" alt="" srcset="https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy.jpg 2160w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy-992x496.jpg 992w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy-1440x720.jpg 1440w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy-768x384.jpg 768w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy-1536x768.jpg 1536w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/fishing-3-copy-2048x1024.jpg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2160px) 100vw, 2160px" /></picture></figure><div class="text-block-with-image__content"><div class="text-block-with-image__inner" style="background-color:#ffffff"><div class="text-block-with-image__text">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">All you need to fish Nevada waters is a pole and a license. Buy your annual or single day license today to get out and explore beautiful parts of the state.</p>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tac"><a href="http://www.ndowlicensing.com" class="cta cta--orange " style="background-color: #e58947">Buy a license now</a></div>



<div class="preparation-plan"><div class="preparation-plan__intro tac"></div><div class="preparation-plan__list accordion">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-accordion-item accordion__item" data-acc="cb53658f-a1e2-4cc4-b84a-8818f209bce5" data-bg="#589fd6" data-aos="" id="accodrion-0"><details><summary>Research </summary><div>
<p class="has-large-font-size wp-block-paragraph">Learn more about fishing in Nevada and how to plan out your trip whether you are new or an experienced angler.</p>



<div class="grid grid--2 grid--small-padding">
<div class="grid__item" data-aos="fade-up">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tal"><a href="/get-outside/fishing/plan-your-fishing-trip" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Plan</a></div>
</div>



<div class="grid__item" data-aos="fade-up">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tal"><a href="/get-outside/fishing/fishing-stocking-reports" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Latest Reports</a></div>
</div>



<div class="grid__item" data-aos="fade-up">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tal"><a href="/species-information" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Find Species</a></div>
</div>



<div class="grid__item" data-aos="fade-up">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tal"><a href="https://fish.wildlifenv.com/" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Interactive Map</a></div>
</div>
</div>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-accordion-item accordion__item" data-acc="6040e164-f39f-44c2-8ed1-798fd4fc37dc" data-bg="#589fd6" data-aos="" id="accodrion-2"><details><summary>Eligibility</summary><div>
<p class="has-large-font-size wp-block-paragraph">People of all ages are allowed to head out to the waters to catch a fish, but anyone 12 years of age or older is required to have a fishing license in their possession while in the field.</p>



<p class="has-large-font-size wp-block-paragraph">If you don’t plan to fish but will be assisting someone (no matter the age), you will be required to have a fishing license.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-accordion-item accordion__item" data-acc="9dcff40d-1570-4a09-965f-e78dcf4d050f" data-bg="#589fd6" data-aos="" id="accodrion-1"><details><summary>License Costs </summary><div>
<p class="activity-list-item__text wp-block-paragraph">Licenses can be purchased online any time of year to head out and fish. License fees are listed below.</p>



<h5 id="specialty-combination-licenses-verification-required" class="wp-block-heading has-small-margin-bottom has-s-m-margin-top has-navy-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-1">Resident Fishing licenses</h5>



<div class="wp-block-group is-nowrap is-layout-flex wp-container-core-group-is-layout-7387b849 wp-block-group-is-layout-flex">
<figure class="wp-block-table has-medium-margin-bottom is-style-regular"><table><tbody><tr><td>Annual Adult Hunt & Fish<br>Combination License <br>(ages 18 & older)</td><td>$75.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Adult Fishing License <br>(ages 18 & older)</td><td>$40.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Youth Hunt & Fish<br>Combination License<br>(ages 12-17)</td><td>$15.00</td></tr><tr><td>1-Day Fishing Permit<br>(ages 18 & older)</td><td>$9.00</td></tr><tr><td>1-Day Fishing Permit<br>Consecutive Day</td><td>$3.00</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>
</div>



<h5 id="nonresident-tag-costs" class="wp-block-heading has-small-margin-bottom has-s-m-margin-top has-navy-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-2">Nonresident fishing licenses</h5>



<div class="wp-block-group is-nowrap is-layout-flex wp-container-core-group-is-layout-7387b849 wp-block-group-is-layout-flex">
<figure class="wp-block-table has-medium-margin-bottom"><table><tbody><tr><td>Annual Adult Fishing License<br>(ages 18 & older)</td><td>$80.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Youth Hunt & Fish <br>Combination License<br>(ages 12-17)</td><td>$15.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Nevada Interstate <br>Boundary Waters License</td><td>$30.00</td></tr><tr><td>1-Day Fishing Permit<br>(ages 18 & older)</td><td>$18.00</td></tr><tr><td>1-Day Fishing Permit<br>Consecutive Day</td><td>$7.00</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>
</div>



<h5 id="nonresident-tag-costs" class="wp-block-heading has-small-margin-bottom has-s-m-margin-top has-navy-color has-text-color has-link-color wp-elements-3">resident Specialty fishing licenses</h5>



<div class="wp-block-group is-nowrap is-layout-flex wp-container-core-group-is-layout-7387b849 wp-block-group-is-layout-flex">
<figure class="wp-block-table has-medium-margin-bottom"><table><tbody><tr><td>Annual Senior Specialty <br>Hunt & Fish Combination License<br>(age 65+ with 6 months residency)</td><td>$15.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Serviceman Specialty <br>Hunt & Fish Combination License*</td><td>$15.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Severely Disabled Specialty<br>Hunt & Fish Combination License**</td><td>$15.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Disabled Veteran Specialty <br>Hunt & Fish Combination License**</td><td>$15.00</td></tr><tr><td>Annual Native American Specialty <br>Hunt & Fish Combination License**</td><td>$10.00</td></tr></tbody></table><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">*Available at NDOW offices only<br>**Initial application must be processed at an NDOW office</figcaption></figure>
</div>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Note: Prices do not include nominal processing fee</p>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tac"><a href="https://nevada.licensing.kalkomey.com/licenses" class="cta cta--orange " style="background-color: #e58947">Buy a license now</a></div>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-accordion-item accordion__item" data-acc="d30bf119-2213-4672-a3c1-81e8e2df8d21" data-bg="#589fd6" data-aos="" id="accodrion-3"><details><summary>Fishing Limits & Seasons </summary><div>
<p class="activity-list-item__text wp-block-paragraph">Find the most recent fishing limits and seasons in your area.</p>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button tal"><a href="https://www.eregulations.com/nevada/fishing " class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Fishing Regulation Book through E-Regulations</a></div>
</div></details></div>
</div></div>
</div></div></div></article>
</div></section>

<article class="featured discover-item text-block-with-image" style="background:none"><figure class="wp-block-image text-block-with-image__image"><picture><img decoding="async" width="1440" height="720" class="wp-image-143 large" loading="lazy" src="https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/boating-education-two-people-in-boat-1440x720.jpeg" alt="" srcset="https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/boating-education-two-people-in-boat-1440x720.jpeg 1440w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/boating-education-two-people-in-boat-992x496.jpeg 992w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/boating-education-two-people-in-boat-768x384.jpeg 768w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/boating-education-two-people-in-boat-1536x768.jpeg 1536w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/boating-education-two-people-in-boat-2048x1024.jpeg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1440px) 100vw, 1440px" /></picture></figure><div class="text-block-with-image__content"><div class="text-block-with-image__inner" style="background-color:#ffffff"><div class="text-block-with-image__text">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph" style="font-size:2.4rem">Whether you’re planning a quick trip close to home or a fishing adventure in Nevada’s backcountry, <a href="https://www.fish.wildlifenv.com/">FishNV</a> can help you find the right place to go. Use the interactive map to explore fishable waters across the state and search by water type, fish species, region or county.</p>
</div></div></div></article>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-container container--small-text container containeru002du002dsmall-text">
<h3 class="wp-block-heading has-text-align-center" id="a-basic-guide-to-fishing-nevada">A Basic Guide to Fishing Nevada</h3>
</div>



<div class="tab-container tab-container--education"><div class="tabs"><div class="tab active">Warmwater Fishing</div><div class="tab">Coldwater Trout Fishing</div></div><div class="tab-panes">
<div class="tab-pane active"><div class="tab-pane__inner tab-pane__inner--full">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-activity-list activity__list">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-activity-list-item activity-list-item" data-aos="true">
<h4 id="where-to-fish" class="wp-block-heading activity-list-item__title">Where to Fish</h4>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Warmwater sport fish are found in ponds, reservoirs, streams and rivers throughout Nevada and generally thrive in water temperatures above 70 degrees. Common species include bluegill, channel and white catfish, largemouth and smallmouth bass, striped bass, white bass, white and black crappie, wiper and yellow perch.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Use FishNV to find waters that contain the species you’re interested in catching.</p>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button left tal"><a href="https://fish.wildlifenv.com/" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Find Fishable Waters</a></div>
</div>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-activity-list-item activity-list-item" data-aos="true">
<h4 id="fishing-tackle" class="wp-block-heading activity-list-item__title">Fishing Tackle</h4>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Warmwater fishing tackle varies depending on the species you’re targeting. Light-action rods with 4- to 8-pound-test line work well for bluegill, crappie, smaller white bass and yellow perch. For larger species such as black bass, channel catfish, striped bass and wiper, consider a medium- to heavy-action rod with 8- to 20-pound-test line.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Fish size can vary by water, so adjust your rod, reel and line accordingly.</p>


</div>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-activity-list-item activity-list-item" data-aos="true">
<h4 id="bait-fishing" class="wp-block-heading activity-list-item__title">Bait Fishing</h4>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bait fishing is a simple and effective way to catch many warmwater fish species. Depending on the species, anglers can fish bait along the bottom or suspend it beneath a bobber.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Popular bait choices include mealworms and red worms for bluegill, small minnows for crappie, nightcrawlers and crayfish for black bass, and prepared baits for catfish. Shad and frozen anchovies are also popular choices for striped bass at lakes Mead and Mohave.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Always review the regulations for the water you plan to fish, as bait restrictions vary by location.</p>


</div>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-activity-list-item activity-list-item" data-aos="true">
<h4 id="lure-fishing" class="wp-block-heading activity-list-item__title">Lure Fishing</h4>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Lures can be an effective way to catch many warmwater fish species. Choose lures that imitate the natural prey found in the water you’re fishing.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Spoons and spinners can trigger strikes through their movement and flash, while crankbaits imitate prey such as minnows and crayfish. Lure size, style and presentation may vary depending on the species, water and time of year.</p>


</div>
</div>
</div></div>



<div class="tab-pane"><div class="tab-pane__inner tab-pane__inner--full">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-activity-list activity__list">
<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-activity-list-item activity-list-item" data-aos="true">
<h4 id="where-to-fish" class="wp-block-heading activity-list-item__title">Where to Fish</h4>



<p class="activity-list-item__text wp-block-paragraph">Coldwater fish species are commonly found in ponds, reservoirs, lakes, streams and rivers throughout Nevada that rarely approach 70 degrees Fahrenheit.  Species generally include brook, brown, cutthroat, lake (or mackinaw) and rainbow trout.  There are also a variety of hybrid trout (tiger or bowcutt) and native mountain whitefish. Many water bodies have self-supporting populations while a good deal of reservoirs and streams are stocked by NDOW with hatchery trout.  Stocking frequently occurs seasonally since late spring and summer water temperatures increase beyond where trout can survive.  We encourage you to check NDOW stocking reports and FishNV for fishable waters containing trout species.</p>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button left tal"><a href="https://fish.wildlifenv.com/" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Find Fishable Waters</a></div>
</div>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-activity-list-item activity-list-item" data-aos="true">
<h4 id="fishing-tackle" class="wp-block-heading activity-list-item__title">Fishing Tackle</h4>



<p class="activity-list-item__text wp-block-paragraph">Since most water bodies fished typically include recently stocked trout, a small light action rod (spinning or bait casting) and line weight from 4 to 8 lb test is ideal.  You may want to move up to a medium action rod with 8 to 12 lb test if you suspect there are bigger fish present.  Fly fishing is also a great way to catch trout, with rod weights and matched fly lines from 3 to 6 the most common choices.</p>


</div>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-activity-list-item activity-list-item" data-aos="true">
<h4 id="bait-fishing" class="wp-block-heading activity-list-item__title">Bait Fishing</h4>



<p class="activity-list-item__text wp-block-paragraph">Bait is very popular for catching trout, is fairly simple, but you must be vigilant and watch your rod for movement. Your bait either sits on the bottom or floats from the surface for an extended time.  You will need hooks, sinkers, and floats (bobbers).  Small hooks such as size 12 or 10 are good for salmon eggs, corn, or scented dough baits (such as Power Bait or Zeke’s) and size 10 to 6 are good for red worms and nightcrawlers.  When fishing on the bottom, it is best to use lighter weights in shallower water and heavier weights in deeper water.  A good variety of hook and weight sizes are good to have on hand so you are covered for any type and situation of fishing.  Bobbers are best used when fish are located close to the surface.  Just pinch a small weight 6 to 12  inches above your hook and adjust the distance of line below the bobber to the depth fish are biting or just above the weedline.  NDOW also provides fishing updates and fish stocking for certain waters around the state, so we encourage you to look at these before heading out.  Finally, it is important to review bait regulations for the water body you plan to fish since the use and type of bait allowed varies.</p>


</div>

<div class="header-with-subtitle"><h2 class="bordered-title" style="color:#19304b" data-aos="true">NDOW Stocking Program</h2></div>



<article class="featured discover-item text-block-with-image" style="background:linear-gradient(to bottom, #ffffff 20.5%, #ffddc4 20.5%)"><figure class="wp-block-image text-block-with-image__image"><picture><img decoding="async" width="1440" height="720" class="wp-image-186 large" loading="lazy" src="https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/ndow-fish-stocking-1440x720.jpeg" alt="" srcset="https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/ndow-fish-stocking-1440x720.jpeg 1440w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/ndow-fish-stocking-992x496.jpeg 992w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/ndow-fish-stocking-768x384.jpeg 768w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/ndow-fish-stocking-1536x768.jpeg 1536w, https://www.ndow.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/ndow-fish-stocking-2048x1024.jpeg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1440px) 100vw, 1440px" /></picture></figure><div class="text-block-with-image__content"><div class="text-block-with-image__inner" style="background-color:#ffddc4"><div class="text-block-with-image__text">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">NDOW operates three fish hatcheries and one fish rearing station across Nevada: Mason Valley Fish Hatchery near Yerington, Gallagher Fish Hatchery in Ruby Valley, Lake Mead Fish Hatchery near Las Vegas and Spring Creek Fish Rearing Station near Baker.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">NDOW hatcheries primarily raise coldwater species, including rainbow, brown and cutthroat trout, to support recreational fishing opportunities throughout the state. Lake Mead Fish Hatchery also helps raise native nongame fish species found in southern Nevada. Warmwater species, including channel catfish, bluegill, wiper and tiger muskie, may also be obtained from other sources for stocking in Nevada waters.</p>



<div class="wp-block-taa-blocks-button buttonWrap left tal"><a href="https://www.ndow.org/get-outside/fishing/fishing-stocking-reports/database/?region=all&show_all=false" class="link link--orange " style="color: #e58947">Find the latest fishing reports and stocking updates here.</a></div>
</div></div></div></article>
</div></section>
